text.en: Dev draws a triangle leaning to the left. He tries to drop a vertical line from the high vertex but finds it meets the base line beyond an endpoint.

An altitude is a perpendicular segment from a vertex to the line containing the opposite side. The meeting point is the foot of the altitude. Extend the opposite side when the perpendicular lands outside the triangle. In a right triangle, two sides serve as altitudes.
Choose a vertex. The side that does not touch it is the opposite side.
Use a set square to draw a perpendicular from the chosen vertex.
Continue the opposite side in a straight line if the perpendicular would miss the side itself.

board.text: Extend if the foot lies outside

text.en: Repeat the construction from each vertex. An altitude can be inside, outside or along a side.

problem.en: How do you construct the altitude from C to the opposite line AB if the foot lies beyond A?

text.en: Extend AB in a straight line beyond A.

why.en: The full base line contains the side and its extension.

text.en: Draw a perpendicular from C to meet the extension at H.

why.en: The segment CH meets the line at a right angle.

prompt.en: Why does the height exist even if it misses the base segment?

requiredIdeas.en: The altitude meets the extended line at 90°.

points.en: An altitude comes from a vertex and meets the opposite line at a right angle.
An obtuse triangle can have an altitude outside it.
